annotation.title_clean: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1107 laying down detailed rules for the continuing airworthiness of certified unmanned aircraft systems and their components, and on the approval of organisations and personnel involved in these tasks
annotation.title_en: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1107 laying down detailed rules for the continuing airworthiness of certified unmanned aircraft systems and their components, and on the approval of organisations and personnel involved in these tasks
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Delegated Regulation 2024/1107 sets continuing airworthiness rules for certified unmanned aircraft systems operated in the 'specific' category, with Part-ML.UAS (owner accountability, maintenance, records, airworthiness review certificates) and Part-CAO.UAS (organisation approval, staff, occurrence reporting, information security). Applies from 1 May 2025.
key_provisions_or_claims: Owner of the UA is accountable for continuing airworthiness; no flight unless airworthy and certificate valid.
Maintenance must be done by Part-CAO.UAS approved organisations with principal place of business in the EU.
Airworthiness review certificate valid 1 year, extendable twice by approved organisations.
Organisations must report occurrences and information security incidents (within 72 hours) to authorities.
Applies from 1 May 2025; CAO.UAS.102 information security from 22 February 2026.
